speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Health what are the financial support schemes available to working care-givers of cancer patients in terms of higher MediSave withdrawal limits, subsidies or tax reliefs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Cancer patients can also tap on MediShield Life and MediSave to pay for both inpatient and outpatient cancer treatments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: To allow families to stretch their combined savings to cover healthcare expenses, care-givers can also use their MediSave to pay for medical expenses incurred by their approved dependants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: It can be used flexibly for care-giving expenses, for example, to hire a foreign domestic worker, for the use of eldercare services, or for transport to medical appointments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Families who need further help with care-giving expenses can approach the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) or Medical Social Workers within healthcare institutions for assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will continue to review and develop initiatives to strengthen support for care-givers.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I just wanted to explain the premise of my question.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There was a 2016 survey in Singapore about general family care-givers, that showed that half of those care-givers were in the economically-active group; they are below 50 years old.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And one in five of those care-givers had to give up their jobs to care for the aged relatives; and one in four reported a worsening of their financial position because of that.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These are the negative eventualities of embarking on this care-giving journey.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I understand that there is no limit for withdrawal from the patients' own MediSave, but would the Ministry also look into increasing the withdrawal limits for care-givers or perhaps also removing any limits for those care-givers for CPF withdrawals for the purposes of assisting in paying for the relative's medical expenses?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think what is important is that if the needs go beyond the current withdrawal limits, the family can approach the Medical Social Worker who will take a look on a case-by-case basis and see how we can  mobilise MediFund, which would then remove the need to touch the MediSave of the care-giver, but yet, let the rest of the taxpayers also do their part to support the needs of this person who is suffering from cancer and who may have extra financial requirements.
